findings.title: Mutating an already-named Django migration to a no-op without its replacement in the same PR
findings.body: The file references `0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py` in its docstring/comment but that migration is not part of this PR. Replacing the body of a migration that is already named and shipped (0917 was generated 2025-04-28, 0920 on 2025-06-03) is dangerous: any environment that recorded an applied state of these migrations will see a hash mismatch when `manage.py migrate` is next run, and any fresh database will silently skip the conversion because 0921 is not present here. Either the coordinating 0921 migration needs to be in this PR, or these files should be left as-is and 0921 should supersede them through the normal Django migration chain (i.e., 0917/0920 must remain non-no-ops, and 0921 must depend on them).

findings.title: Mutating an already-named Django migration to a no-op without its replacement in the same PR
findings.body: Same issue as 0917: the comment refers to `0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py` which is not in this PR, and the migration body has been reduced to `return`. If any environment has applied 0920, Django will refuse to continue and may require manual intervention; if no environment has applied it, this still relies on a migration (0921) that the reviewer cannot inspect, and the corresponding test for the conversion has been removed without a replacement test for 0921.

findings.title: TableWidgetVisualization is rendered with empty columns and empty data when the feature flag is on
findings.body: Inside `tableResultComponent`, when `organization.features.includes('use-table-widget-visualization')` is true, `<TableWidgetVisualization>` is rendered with `columns={[]}` and `tableData={{ data: [], meta: { fields: {}, units: {} } }}`, ignoring the actual `result.data` and `result.meta` (and `fieldAliases`, `fields`, `fieldHeaderMap`, etc. used by the legacy path). For any organization with this feature flag enabled, every table widget in a dashboard will render as an empty table. There is also no test covering the feature-flag-enabled branch. The gated branch should pass the real `result.data`, `result.meta`, and columns derived from `result.meta.fields` (and any `fieldAliases`/`fieldHeaderMap`/`getCustomFieldRenderer`) rather than hard-coded empty values.

findings.title: Analytics recorded before authorization check
findings.body: `analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` is invoked at the top of `post`, before the `features.has("organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble", ...)` gate and before any other validation (schema validation, chunk upload checks, etc.). This means every POST to this endpoint — including unauthorized, malformed, and feature-flag-disabled requests — will be counted in the analytics event, skewing usage data and breaking any downstream dashboards or alerting on this event. The analytics call should be moved to after the feature flag check and ideally after the request has been validated as legitimate.

findings.title: Default for sentry:autofix_automation_tuning changed from "low" to "off" without an opt-in rollout
findings.body: `DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT` changed from "low" to "off", and the project option default (`src/sentry/projectoptions/defaults.py`) was updated to match. This silently changes behavior for any project that was relying on the previous default of "low". Combined with the existing feature flag handling in `test_project_details.py`/`test_project.py` which now assert the new default, this is a behavior change shipped in the same release as the code rather than a controlled rollout. Projects that have never explicitly set this option will see autofix turned off after deploy, which is a user-visible behavior change that should either require an explicit upgrade step or be gated behind a flag.

findings.title: Visualize constructor signature changed from (yAxes[], options) to (yAxis, options)
findings.body: `Visualize` previously accepted `yAxes: readonly string[]` and stored an array of y-axes per visualize. It now requires a single `yAxis: string`. While the in-tree callers have been updated, this is an exported public class used by getsentry and other downstream consumers. Any external code constructing `new Visualize(["count()", "avg()"], {...})` will now pass an array as the first argument and the class will store the array as a string (TypeScript will likely error or, worse, silently misbehave). Either keep both shapes via a deprecated overload, document this as a breaking change in a changelog/release notes, or guard with a runtime check that throws a clear error for the old shape.

findings.title: get_environment_info swallows all exceptions via bare `except Exception`
findings.body: `get_environment_info` catches `Exception` for the entire `issue.get_recommended_event()` + `recommended_event.get_environment()` block and logs the error as `info` rather than `warning`/`error`. This hides genuine failures (DB outages, programming errors, schema drift) behind a benign-looking info log and degrades the new PR comment feature silently. The try/except should at minimum scope the catch (e.g., only catch expected lookup misses / `Group.DoesNotExist`-style failures) and the unexpected branch should log at warning or re-raise so issues surface in Sentry.

findings.title: dcg_to_slow_conditions now keyed by dcg_ids instead of dcg_to_groups.keys()
findings.body: `get_condition_query_groups` previously computed `dcg_to_slow_conditions` from `event_data.dcg_to_groups.keys()` and looked up `dcg_to_slow_conditions[dcg.id]` for every dcg in `data_condition_groups` (which is fetched from `event_data.dcg_ids`). After the refactor, the slow-conditions dict is built once from `event_data.dcg_ids` and reused in both `get_condition_query_groups` and `get_groups_to_fire`. The new behavior is more correct (it now covers DCGs present in `dcg_ids` but missing from `dcg_to_groups`, which would previously have raised `KeyError`), but it changes the set of condition groups considered "slow". Any DCG that previously was not flagged as slow because it was missing from `dcg_to_groups.keys()` will now be flagged as slow, potentially altering which conditions get sent to Snuba and which workflows fire. Worth verifying with a sample trace that this matches the intended semantics.

findings.title: Fallback column derivation reads meta.fields with no null check
findings.body: When `columns` is not provided, the fallback computes `Object.keys(tableData?.meta.fields).map(...)`. The optional chaining handles `tableData` being undefined but does not handle `tableData.meta` itself being undefined — if a caller passes `tableData` without a `meta` key (or with `meta: undefined`), this throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'fields')`. This becomes very real given that `chart.tsx` is calling this component with `tableData.meta` set, but downstream callers may forget. Use `tableData?.meta?.fields` for the safe default.

findings.title: PR comment template no longer includes the issue culprit/subtitle
findings.body: The previous comment format was `- ‼️ **{title}** \`{subtitle}\` [View Issue]({url})`, which surfaced the issue's `culprit` (the file/function associated with the issue). The new template is `* ‼️ [**{title}**]({url}){environment}\n` and replaces the subtitle with an environment tag. Anyone scanning PR comments to find which file triggered an issue loses that information. If the subtitle was noisy or low-value, that's fine, but this is a deliberate change to user-visible PR content and should be called out in release notes.

findings.title: schedule_webhook_delivery given a 30s processing_deadline_duration
findings.body: `schedule_webhook_delivery` is the parent task that fans out delivery tasks to `drain_mailbox`. 30s is a tight budget for a task that may need to schedule a large batch of webhook deliveries (Redis push, multiple apply_async calls, potentially across many integrations). If the task exceeds 30s the in-flight work is killed by the taskworker, leaving deliveries unscheduled. Consider a more generous budget (e.g., 5–10 minutes consistent with `drain_mailbox`) or chunk the dispatch into smaller batches.

findings.title: Per-error nodestore lookup not batched
findings.body: `fetch_error_details` does `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` which is batched, but for each issue the broader flow calls `issue.get_recommended_event()` (separate Eventstore lookup) inside `fetch_error_details` would be one DB query per error. In `make_seer_request` the actual call passes the full log list at once, so the prompt is fine, but `fetch_error_details` itself iterates and calls `Event.generate_node_id` for each error id; if error_ids is large this is N independent DB reads per call site. Not a blocker but worth a follow-up to batch event lookups.

findings.title: max_segment_id null guard could mask the same bug elsewhere
findings.body: `_make_recording_filenames` now early-returns `[]` when `row["max_segment_id"] is None`, and the TypedDict was widened from `int` to `int | None`. The accompanying test (`tests/sentry/replays/tasks/test_delete_replays_bulk.py`) was updated to match. This is a defensive fix, but a `max_segment_id` of None on a real replay row is data the bulk-delete query should be filtering out upstream (via `WHERE max(segment_id) IS NOT NULL`) rather than producing rows that silently delete nothing. Verify that the Snuba query in `fetch_rows_matching_pattern` excludes or filters these rows so the caller doesn't keep paging through hundreds of empty results.
